title: In silico and in vitro analysis of PPAR - alpha / gamma dual agonists: Comparative evaluation of potential phytochemicals with anti-obesity drug orlistat.
authors: Mandal, Sumit Kumar; Kumar, Banoth Karan; Sharma, Pankaj Kumar; Murugesan, Sankaranarayanan; Deepa, P R
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子对接和MD模拟评估植物化学物与PPAR核受体的结合，虽涉及转录因子配体结合，但核心是药物筛选而非TF-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法创新，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: Obesity is an abnormal fat accumulation disorder in the metabolic syndrome constellation, and a risk factor for diabetes, cardiovascular disorders, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and cancer. Nuclear receptors (Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor, PPAR) are implicated in metabolic syndrome and NAFLD, and have potential for therapeutic targeting. Nuclear receptors are ligand-dependent transcription factors that have diverse roles in metabolism, including regulating genes involved in lipid and glucose metabolism, modulating inflammatory genes, and are crucial for maintaining metabolic flexibility. PPAR activates adipose triglyceride lipase, which then releases fatty acids as ligands for PPAR, indicating the interdependency of nuclear receptors and lipases. Here, molecular docking was performed with selected phytochemical ligands that can bind with PPAR-alpha/gamma (PDB ID: 2ZNN and 2ATH, respectively) using Glide module of Schrodinger software followed by molecular dynamics simulation study using Desmond module, and ADMET analysis. Interestingly, orlistat which is a well-known lipase and fatty acid synthase inhibitor also demonstrated favorable binding affinity with both PPAR-alpha/gamma (-10.96 kcal/mol against PPARalpha and -10.26 kcal/mol against PPARgamma). The highest docking scores were however shown by the flavonoids - rutin (-14.88 kcal/mol against PPARalpha and -13.64 kcal/mol against PPARgamma), and its aglycone, quercetin (-10.08 kcal/mol in PPARalpha and -9.89 kcal/mol in PPARgamma). The other phytochemicals (genistein, esculin, daidzin, naringenin, daidzein, dihydroxy coumarin, hydroquinone) showed lower binding affinity as dual agonists. The anti-obesity effects were experimentally validated in cultured adipocytes, which revealed better lipid inhibition by rutin and quercetin than orlistat (quercetin > rutin > orlistat) pointing to their strong potential in anti-obesity treatment.
abstract_zh: 肥胖是代谢综合征范畴内的一种异常脂肪堆积性疾病，也是糖尿病、心血管疾病、非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）和癌症的风险因素。核受体（过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体，PPAR）与代谢综合征和NAFLD相关，并具有治疗靶向的潜力。核受体是配体依赖性转录因子，在代谢中发挥多种作用，包括调控参与脂质和葡萄糖代谢的基因、调节炎症基因，并且对维持代谢灵活性至关重要。PPAR激活脂肪组织甘油三酯脂肪酶，该酶随后释放脂肪酸作为PPAR的配体，表明核受体与脂肪酶之间的相互依赖性。在此，使用Schrodinger软件的Glide模块对选定的植物化学配体进行分子对接，这些配体可与PPAR-α/γ（PDB ID分别为2ZNN和2ATH）结合，随后使用Desmond模块进行分子动力学模拟研究，并进行ADMET分析。有趣的是，奥利司他（一种众所周知的脂肪酶和脂肪酸合酶抑制剂）也显示出与PPAR-α/γ的良好结合亲和力（对PPARα为-10.96 kcal/mol，对PPARγ为-10.26 kcal/mol）。然而，最高对接分数由黄酮类化合物芦丁（对PPARα为-14.88 kcal/mol，对PPARγ为-13.64 kcal/mol）及其苷元槲皮素（对PPARα为-10.08 kcal/mol，对PPARγ为-9.89 kcal/mol）显示。其他植物化学物质（染料木黄酮、秦皮甲素、大豆苷、柚皮素、大豆苷元、二羟基香豆素、氢醌）作为双重激动剂显示出较低的结合亲和力。抗肥胖效应在培养的脂肪细胞中进行了实验验证，结果显示芦丁和槲皮素对脂质的抑制作用优于奥利司他（槲皮素 > 芦丁 > 奥利司他），表明它们在抗肥胖治疗中具有强大潜力。
